findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff defines `self.downsize` twice in the same class; Ruby silently keeps the last definition, so the first one is dead code and callers expecting the (from, to, max_width, max_height) signature call the wrong method. The 4-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)` at the top is completely overridden by the later 3-argument `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`; any existing caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 200)` hits the second definition, binding `dimensions=100` and `opts=200`, then passes `100` where a dimensions string is expected — raising a TypeError (no implicit conversion of Integer into String) or producing a broken command, breaking every existing thumbnail/resized-image generation path that calls downsize with width/height.

[BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` passes the string "80%" as the `dimensions` argument, but `downsize_instructions`/`downsize_instructions_animated` parse dimensions in "WxH" form. `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions(from, to, "80%", opts)`, which does `dimensions.split("x")` (e.g. expecting "100x100"); with "80%" this either raises a NoMethodError/wrong-arity inside the instructions builder or emits an invalid ImageMagick command, so the downsize loop never reduces the file and uploads over the limit still fail with the original error (or a 500 from the raised exception, which is not rescued).

[BUG] The downsize call uses the same tempfile path as both source and destination (`tempfile.path, tempfile.path`), so ImageMagick `convert` is asked to read and write the identical file. `convert_with` runs a shell `convert in.png out.png`; with input and output the same path, ImageMagick either refuses (exit != 0, leaving the file unchanged so the loop spins 5 times uselessly and the upload still fails the size check) or reads a truncated/zero-length file mid-write, corrupting the user's upload before `Upload.create_for` persists it.

[ADVISORY] The client-side max size check is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB, discarding the `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` site setting it previously read, while the server still enforces the actual setting. Admins who set max_image_size_kb to e.g. 512 KB get no client-side warning until the server rejects the upload, and users uploading a 9 MB image are told 10 MB is the limit even when the feature intends to auto-downsize — the error message in the 413 handler likewise lies about the real limit for every site that changes the setting.

[BUG] The downsize loop passes tempfile.path as both source and destination, which ImageMagick's convert rejects because it cannot read and write the same file in one invocation. OptimizedImage.downsize returns false (or produces a truncated/corrupt file) on every iteration; the loop burns all 5 attempts, tempfile.size never shrinks, and the upload proceeds at original size — the feature silently never downsizes anything, and the file may be corrupted mid-loop leaving the user with a broken upload instead of a clear size error.

[BUG] The loop calls downsize with "80%" as the dimensions argument, but downsize_instructions (and its animated variant) generate a geometry string from that argument expecting a WxH form; the animated path additionally only engages when the source filename ends in .GIF, which a tempfile named "discourse-upload-<type>" never does. Animated GIFs above max_image_size_kb get downsized via the non-animated single-frame path with a percent geometry the instructions builder wasn't written for, so users uploading large animated images get a single frozen frame or an over-size file instead of the intended reduced animated image.

[BUG] The loop has no success verification: after 5 iterations of 80% (≈32% area reduction) the tempfile can still exceed max_image_size_kb, yet the code unconditionally proceeds to Upload.create_for. A 100MB image on a site with max_image_size_kb=512 is still ~10MB after 5 passes; the user who was promised automatic reduction gets an opaque server-side validation failure instead of either more aggressive downsizing or a clear error.

[BUG] The client-side max size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type, discarding the per-type SiteSetting lookup that previously distinguished max_image_size_kb from max_attachment_size_kb. Non-image attachments: (a) sites with max_attachment_size_kb < 10MB lose the friendly client-side pre-check and hit the server 413 instead; (b) sites with a limit above 10MB get a false 'file too large' rejection in the browser for files the server would accept — a silent functional regression for attachment-heavy communities.

[BUG] The 413 error handler hardcodes 10MB as the reported maximum, so the error message shown to the user no longer matches the limit the server actually enforces. On sites where max_attachment_size_kb or max_image_size_kb differ from 10MB, users are told a wrong limit in the 'file too large' dialog, and the message cannot be corrected without a client code deploy even though the underlying setting is site-configurable.

[BUG] The API URL-download path replaces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb with a hardcoded 10.megabytes download cap for all types, including non-image uploads pulled via URL. API clients downloading attachments by URL on sites with limits above 10MB get truncated downloads (FileHelper.download enforces the cap) and silent upload failures; the previous per-site configurability is lost with no flag or setting to restore it.

[ADVISORY] The diff redefines def self.downsize twice in the same module (line ~142 with (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) and the new (from, to, dimensions, opts)); the second definition silently shadows the first, and existing callers passing width/height as separate args now bind max_width to the width and to to the height, producing geometry strings like "640x" from previously-valid calls. Any pre-existing caller of OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h) elsewhere in the codebase (thumbnail generation paths) now generates a malformed geometry and broken thumbnails; the dead first definition also guarantees the next editor reads two conflicting signatures.

[ADVISORY] The new automatic-downsize behavior — new non-trivial logic including a retry loop, a percent geometry, animation handling, and an over-limit fallback — ships with zero test coverage: the diff contains no spec file, no *_spec.rb changes, and no assertions touching the downsize loop. The in-place-write failure, the animated-GIF extension mismatch, and the 5-attempt exhaustion described in sibling findings all ship to production unverified; a regression in any of them blocks every large-image upload on the site with no test to catch it pre-merge.

[ADVISORY] The image check uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename), where filename comes from the user-supplied original filename (or a URL basename) rather than the downloaded tempfile's actual content type. A user who renames a non-image file to .png, or a URL whose path lacks an image extension, bypasses or spuriously triggers the downsize loop; non-image payloads renamed as images are handed to convert, which either fails silently or wastes 5 convert invocations per upload attempt.

[BUG] The downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the string "80%" as its dimensions argument, which is not a valid WxH dimension spec. The generated ImageMagick instruction receives a malformed geometry ('80%' where 'WxH' is expected), so the downsize either fails every iteration (silently swallowed by the `&> /dev/null` convert) leaving the tempfile unchanged, or is interpreted as a percentage-resize the instructions builder doesn't produce — either way the loop burns 5 convert subprocess spawns per oversized upload and the upload still fails with the original size error. The feature does not work at all for its stated purpose.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both from and to, mutating the original upload in place. When (if) downsizing works, the user's original full-resolution image is permanently destroyed server-side before Upload.create_for, with no backup — the feature's requirement was to 'allow large images by reducing them', but in-place mutation means data loss of the original and no rollback if Upload.create_for then fails (e.g. non-image content-type mismatch).

[BUG] The client-side max size check replaces the admin-configurable SiteSetting (max_image_size_kb / per-type max_X_size_kb) with a hardcoded 10MB constant. Every site's configured upload limits are silently ignored client-side: an admin who set max_image_size_kb to 500KB sees users pass the client gate and get server-side rejections (or unwanted server-side re-encoding they explicitly disallowed); an admin who raised the limit above 10MB sees users blocked at 10MB despite the server accepting larger files. This is untraceable to the stated feature intent and silently removes an operator control.

[BUG] The API URL-download path hardcodes 10.megabytes instead of the configurable limit, replacing SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. API uploads from URLs larger than the site's configured max but under 10MB are now downloaded and then silently re-encoded by the new downsize loop, even on sites whose admins set max_image_size_kb to 0 (unlimited) — wait, the loop guards on >0, but the download cap itself now ignores the setting, so admins who raised the limit above 10MB can no longer fetch such URLs.

[ADVISORY] The 413 error handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB to the user even when the server rejected based on a different (smaller) configured limit. Users get a misleading error message naming a limit the site doesn't actually enforce; this is scope drift — fixing the error message was not required to downsize large images.

[BUG] The class defines self.downsize twice — the original two-argument (max_width, max_height) method at line 142 is immediately overridden by a new dimensions-string variant at line 148. Ruby silently keeps the last definition, so the new signature wins; but every pre-existing caller of downsize that passes (width, height) as two integers now has them interpolated as "#{width}x#{height}" — that happens to match, but any caller passing opts differently or relying on the old arity contract is on a silent behavior change, and the dead first definition is a maintenance trap (a future editor will edit the wrong one). Parallel duplicate method definitions with diverging signatures is untraceable to any requirement in this feature.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop runs up to 5 unconditional ImageMagick subprocess spawns per oversized upload with no failure detection (convert_with's false return is ignored) and no check that the file is even a decodable image by content. On every upload between max_image_size_kb and 10MB the server burns up to 5 sequential convert processes even when the first fails (e.g. a misnamed .png that isn't an image), degrading upload latency and offering a subprocess-spawn vector per request; the per-iteration failure is invisible to both operator and user.

[BUG] The diff defines `def self.downsize` twice — the second definition (taking a single `dimensions` string) shadows the first, so every existing four-argument call site `downsize(from, to, width, height)` now binds width into `dimensions` and height into `opts`, producing malformed geometry. Any existing caller passing width and height separately (the classic Discourse avatar/thumb resize paths) generates a geometry string like "100" instead of "100x200", so ImageMagick either resizes to the wrong dimensions or fails silently, corrupting every derived image on that path; the first definition's new string-interpolation change is also dead code, hiding the bug.

[BUG] The downsize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` on `tempfile.path` for both `from` and `to`, writing ImageMagick's output onto its own input file in place. When the ImageMagick invocation fails or truncates mid-conversion (convert_to a same-file target), the original upload file is destroyed or corrupted, and the loop then keeps re-converting a now-broken file up to 5 times before passing the damaged tempfile to Upload.create_for — the user's original image data is lost with no recovery path.

[BUG] The loop terminates after 5 attempts with no success check and no handling of `convert_with` returning false, then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` unconditionally. A large image that cannot reach max_image_size_kb in 5 × 20% reductions (e.g. a 40MB PNG against a 1MB setting shrinks only to ~13MB) still gets submitted, and since server-side validation still rejects it, the user gets a file-too-large error only after five synchronous shell conversions have burned CPU — and an animated GIF whose conversion fails outright is re-run 5 times on an unchanged file before failing anyway.

[BUG] The animated-image branch in `optimize` triggers on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but the passed path is a Rails tempfile (e.g. `/tmp/discourse-upload-image` or an uploaded tempfile with no `.gif` extension), so the pattern never matches and animated images take the still-image instruction path. Animated GIF uploads above the size limit get flattened to a single frame (or stripped entirely by the non-animated pipeline), silently losing animation even though `allow_animated_thumbnails` was explicitly passed to permit it.

[ADVISORY] The client-side check hardcodes `10 * 1024` KB and drops the per-type lookup `SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, creating a duplicated limit with no single source of truth. Non-image types (attachments, avatars) now pass client validation up to 10MB even when their server-side `max_attachment_size_kb`/`max_avatar_size_kb` is far lower, so users get a server-side rejection after a full upload instead of the instant client-side alert; and if an admin raises `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB, files between 10MB and the setting are rejected client-side that the server would now accept and downsize — the two limits have already drifted in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The API download cap is hardcoded to `10.megabytes`, decoupled from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` that the downsize logic one line below depends on. An admin raising max_image_size_kb above 10MB gets API-URL uploads silently truncated/failed by the download cap while form uploads of the same size succeed — two limits that must agree are enforced in different places with different values.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop runs inside the request cycle, executing up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick shell-outs before the upload is even created. A client uploading many large images concurrently (or a scripted API client) makes each request hold a worker for the duration of 5 full-image conversions, so image-heavy traffic exhausts the web worker pool and degrades all tenants on the site — the hot path has no async/job offload or size cap before conversion.

[BUG] The client-side max-size check silently discards the admin-configurable SiteSetting and hardcodes 10MB, changing the feature's objective from 'enforce the site's configured upload limit' to 'enforce a fixed 10MB limit' without any human acceptance of that policy change. On sites where max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb is set below 10240 KB, files between the site limit and 10MB pass the client check and are rejected by the server with a generic error; on sites configured above 10MB, users are incorrectly blocked client-side with an error quoting a limit that no longer matches any real configuration.

[BUG] The 413 error handler now always tells the user the limit is 10MB regardless of the actual server-configured limit. When the server rejects with 413 under a different max_image_size_kb setting, the user is shown an explicit wrong number ('max 10 MB') that does not match the real limit, so they resize to 10MB and are rejected again with no actionable guidance.

[BUG] The API URL-download size cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, silently overriding the SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb the code previously enforced, so server-side policy is no longer honored for this path. Admins who lower or raise max_image_size_kb have no effect on API-driven URL uploads: oversized remote images are downloaded up to a fixed 10MB and then either rejected with a mismatched error or, combined with the new downsize loop, silently resized despite the admin intending a smaller cap; this policy change was not part of the stated feature intent.

[BUG] The new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 145-148 is a duplicate method definition that shadows the two-argument-dimensions version defined immediately above at lines 143-144, so the earlier definition is dead code and all existing callers invoking downsize(from, to, width, height) now hit the new signature. Existing call sites that pass downsize(from, to, 600, 300) now bind dimensions=600 and opts=300, producing the geometry string '600' (a lone width) instead of '600x300', so images are resized to an unintended geometry — a silent behavior change to OptimizedImage's public API introduced by refactoring rather than by the feature's intent.

[ADVISORY] The new server-side downsize loop accepts any image up to 10MB (per the hardcoded client cap) and iteratively shrinks it to fit max_image_size_kb, which inverts the original contract that uploads exceeding the site limit are rejected with a clear error. Users uploading a 10MB image get a silently re-encoded, quality-degraded upload (up to 5 lossy 80% passes) with no notification that their file was altered; admins who relied on the size limit as a hard guarantee (e.g. bandwidth/storage policy) now have it bypassed for any image type, and the loop exits after 5 attempts even if the file is still over the limit, at which point it is passed to Upload.create_for anyway.

[BUG] The size-limit enforcement is now best-effort, allowing uploads that exceed the admin-configured max_image_size_kb. The downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations at "80%" each (max ~33% reduction); a 10MB image against a 1MB limit stays over the limit after 5 attempts and is then passed to Upload.create_for anyway — and if OptimizedImage.downsize fails (non-decodable file, ImageMagick error), the tempfile is unchanged and upload proceeds at full size. Admins lose the hard size ceiling; disk/bandwidth DoS vector via repeated near-10MB uploads.

[BUG] Image detection is based on the client-controlled filename rather than verified content, so the downsize step is bypassable and the client-declared content_type is trusted. FileHelper.is_image?(filename) checks an extension taken from File.basename(URI.parse(url).path) on the API path or the multipart filename — a user renames a 10MB non-image payload to .png, skips downsizing entirely (no size reduction, and ImageMagick never processes it), and uploads it with a self-declared content_type of image/png; the server-side max-image-size policy is defeated for any file with a spoofed extension, and the trust-the-client content_type flows into Upload.create_for.

[BUG] Hardcoding the client-side limit to 10MB bypasses the site's configured upload-size settings for all upload types, not just images. max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb (and any other per-type *_size_kb setting) are ignored client-side: on a site configured with max_attachment_size_kb = 512, users select attachments up to 10MB and push them at the server; combined with the server's downsizing only applying to image filenames, oversized non-image attachments that previously were rejected now transit the full upload path. An admin-configured control is silently disabled.

[ADVISORY] The new public downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) signature interpolates a caller-supplied raw dimensions string into a shell command via convert_with's backticks, removing the structured width/height parameterization the old dimensions(width, height) builder provided. In this diff dimensions is the literal "80%" so it is safe today, but the method's contract change means any future caller that forwards user-influenced geometry (e.g. a user-specified crop or resize string) gets direct command injection into `#{instructions.join(" ")}`; the deletion of the width/height typed parameters is what creates the injection-shaped API.

[ADVISORY] The file defines self.downsize twice (the 4-arg (max_width, max_height) version is immediately shadowed by the dimensions version), so existing callers passing separate width and height integers now hit the wrong parameterization. Any existing call site of OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 100) now binds dimensions=100 and opts=100 instead of building "100x100"; the mutated image paths this controls (thumbnails/resized avatars) silently corrupt geometry handling for the next maintainer who cannot tell which overload is live — a change-safety hazard the duplicate definition hides.

[ADVISORY] The API URL-download path fetches a user-supplied URL with only a size cap and rescue nil, and the diff widens that fetch budget from the configured max_image_size_kb to a fixed 10MB regardless of the site's setting. An API user triggers server-side fetches of arbitrary URLs (SSRF surface already present, but the budget is now decoupled from admin configuration), and the rescue nil swallows fetch failures leaving tempfile nil while filename/URI.parse(url) still runs on the raw user URL — a malformed URI raises after the rescue, producing a 500 on attacker-chosen input.

[BUG] `downsize` is defined twice in the same class body; the second definition (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) silently overwrites the first (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}), so any existing caller still invoking the old 5-argument form mis-binds `max_height` into `opts` and `dimensions` becomes only the width string. Any out-of-diff caller doing OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 100) now executes downsize_instructions with dimensions="100" (height lost, opts={100 => true}), producing wrongly-sized optimized images with no error — a silent behavior regression in every existing downsize call site.

[BUG] The downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize but discards its return value, and convert_with returns false on ImageMagick failure, so the loop retries 5 times against the same unshrunk file and then falls through to Upload.create_for with an oversized tempfile. When ImageMagick fails (corrupt image, missing binary, unsupported format), the user waits through 5 pointless shell invocations and then receives a generic upload failure instead of the file_too_large message the client now promises at 10MB — the failure mode the loop was written to prevent still occurs, just slower.

[BUG] downsize is invoked with `tempfile.path` as both `from` and `to` (in-place), so an ImageMagick run that fails midway overwrites/truncates the original tempfile before failure is detected. A partially-converted or zero-byte file is handed to Upload.create_for, which either fails with a confusing content-type/size error or stores a corrupted image — the user's original upload is destroyed by the very code meant to help them.

[ADVISORY] The client hardcodes `10 * 1024` as the max size, replacing the SiteSetting-driven value, so the client-side alert no longer reflects the server's actual `max_image_size_kb` (which can be any value, including 0 = unlimited). Admins who set max_image_size_kb above or below 10MB get a wrong number shown to every user; users uploading a 12MB image of a type not covered by the server downsize path (non-image, or max_image_size_kb == 0) pass the client check and then hit a server rejection with a mismatched error message.

[ADVISORY] The API download branch names the tempfile `discourse-upload-#{type}` with no image extension, so inside `optimize` the animated-GIF detection `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` never matches for URL-provided uploads and `allow_animation` is silently ignored there. Animated GIFs downloaded via API URL take the non-animated instruction path, producing a still or wrongly-processed image with no error surfaced — a hidden branch divergence between file uploads and URL uploads that no test distinguishes.

[BUG] The class now defines self.downsize twice — the original (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) version at ~line 146 is immediately shadowed by a new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version at ~line 150 — so every existing caller that invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts) with four positional arguments raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 4 for 3) because the last definition wins. Any pre-existing thumbnail-generation code path that calls downsize with the old 4-arg signature crashes at runtime with an unhandled ArgumentError instead of producing the resized image — thumbnail generation for those call sites is broken with no fallback.

[BUG] The client-side size check hard-codes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 instead of the site setting, so the composer rejects any file over 10MB with 'file too large' before the request is ever sent — but the entire point of the new server-side loop in uploads_controller.rb is to accept larger images and downsize them automatically. The feature is dead on arrival for its target users: a user uploading a 30MB image is blocked client-side by bootbox.alert and never reaches the server-side downsizing code; additionally, any site with max_image_size_kb above 10MB (or non-image types with larger limits) silently regresses — uploads the server previously accepted are now refused with a wrong limit shown in the error message.

[BUG] The downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...) with from == to — the same path is passed as both source and destination, so the ImageMagick command reads and writes the same file in place. ImageMagick's convert reading and writing the identical path can produce a truncated/corrupt output (the reader may consume the file while the writer truncates it), so the upload proceeds with a corrupted image or, if the convert fails outright, the original oversized file — either way the user gets a broken upload or a confusing file_too_large error after the loop silently exhausts all 5 attempts.

[ADVISORY] The loop ignores the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (convert_with returns false when the shell command exits non-zero) and performs no check after the loop, so a failing convert is retried four more times against the unchanged file and then execution falls through to Upload.create_for with the still-oversized tempfile. A corrupt or non-processable image that fails convert burns 5 shell invocations with no log and no early exit, then surfaces only as a generic 'file too large' error at upload creation — the operator gets no signal that downsizing itself failed, and the user sees a misleading error for what is actually an image-processing failure.

[ADVISORY] The 413 response handler now hard-codes 10MB as the reported max size, disconnecting the displayed limit from the server's actual configured max_image_size_kb. Users on sites where max_image_size_kb differs from 10240 are shown a wrong limit in the file_too_large alert, misdirecting them about what they need to do to fix the upload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side max-size check silently discards the admin-configurable SiteSetting and hardcodes 10MB, changing the feature's objective from 'enforce the site's configured upload limit' to 'enforce a fixed 10MB limit' without any human acceptance of that policy change. On sites where max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb is set below 10240 KB, files between the site limit and 10MB pass the client check and are rejected by the server with a generic error; on sites configured above 10MB, users are incorrectly blocked client-side with an error quoting a limit that no longer matches any real configuration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces the client-side size limit derived from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in two places in `utilities.js`. This removes enforcement of admin-configured limits on the client, creating mismatches where configured limits differ from 10MB (either allowing uploads that the server may reject, or blocking uploads that the site configuration would allow).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 413 error handler now always tells the user the limit is 10MB regardless of the actual server-configured limit. When the server rejects with 413 under a different max_image_size_kb setting, the user is shown an explicit wrong number ('max 10 MB') that does not match the real limit, so they resize to 10MB and are rejected again with no actionable guidance.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js`, the 413 handler was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means the user-facing error message will always report 10MB even if the server/upload limit is configured differently, which can mislead users after a real 413 response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The API URL-download size cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, silently overriding the SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb the code previously enforced, so server-side policy is no longer honored for this path. Admins who lower or raise max_image_size_kb have no effect on API-driven URL uploads: oversized remote images are downloaded up to a fixed 10MB and then either rejected with a mismatched error or, combined with the new downsize loop, silently resized despite the admin intending a smaller cap; this policy change was not part of the stated feature intent.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API URL-download path changed from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to a hardcoded `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`, so `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` no longer controls the download cap for remote/API URL uploads. This is a behavioral/config-policy regression visible in the diff (and also prevents downloading images larger than 10MB even if the setting is higher). The new downsize loop later uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, but it does not restore the setting-controlled download limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 145-148 is a duplicate method definition that shadows the two-argument-dimensions version defined immediately above at lines 143-144, so the earlier definition is dead code and all existing callers invoking downsize(from, to, width, height) now hit the new signature. Existing call sites that pass downsize(from, to, 600, 300) now bind dimensions=600 and opts=300, producing the geometry string '600' (a lone width) instead of '600x300', so images are resized to an unintended geometry — a silent behavior change to OptimizedImage's public API introduced by refactoring rather than by the feature's intent.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined and then immediately redefined as `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, so the first version becomes dead code (Ruby last definition wins). This changes the method arity/meaning: existing callers passing `(from, to, width, height)` will now bind `dimensions=width` and `opts=height`, and `optimize` then does `opts[:allow_animation]`, which will error (e.g., TypeError/NoMethodError) when `opts` is an Integer, or otherwise behave incorrectly. This is a real behavioral break introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new server-side downsize loop accepts any image up to 10MB (per the hardcoded client cap) and iteratively shrinks it to fit max_image_size_kb, which inverts the original contract that uploads exceeding the site limit are rejected with a clear error. Users uploading a 10MB image get a silently re-encoded, quality-degraded upload (up to 5 lossy 80% passes) with no notification that their file was altered; admins who relied on the size limit as a hard guarantee (e.g. bandwidth/storage policy) now have it bypassed for any image type, and the loop exits after 5 attempts even if the file is still over the limit, at which point it is passed to Upload.create_for anyway.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes enforcement/UX around size limits: the client-side max is hardcoded to 10*1024 KB (10MB) instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings[...]` in `utilities.js`, and API URL downloads are capped at `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` in `uploads_controller.rb`. Server-side, a new loop conditionally re-encodes images (`OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`) up to 5 times to try to get under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, but after the loop there is no explicit check to reject if the tempfile is still over the limit before calling `Upload.create_for(...)`. Whether this is a "bug" depends on intended product behavior (allow oversize images to be downscaled), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded concern: settings are bypassed/altered and the code doesn’t guarantee the post-condition (<= max) nor notify the user about modification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The size-limit enforcement is now best-effort, allowing uploads that exceed the admin-configured max_image_size_kb. The downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations at "80%" each (max ~33% reduction); a 10MB image against a 1MB limit stays over the limit after 5 attempts and is then passed to Upload.create_for anyway — and if OptimizedImage.downsize fails (non-decodable file, ImageMagick error), the tempfile is unchanged and upload proceeds at full size. Admins lose the hard size ceiling; disk/bandwidth DoS vector via repeated near-10MB uploads.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new “best-effort” downsize loop (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes ...`) has no post-condition check: if downsizing fails or the file remains above the configured limit after 5 iterations, the code still calls `Upload.create_for(...)` with the (potentially still-oversized) tempfile. The diff itself does not show whether `Upload.create_for` enforces `max_image_size_kb`, so the stronger claim that admins “lose the hard size ceiling” and that oversized uploads are accepted cannot be verified from this diff alone. However, the missing explicit enforcement/handling after the loop is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Image detection is based on the client-controlled filename rather than verified content, so the downsize step is bypassable and the client-declared content_type is trusted. FileHelper.is_image?(filename) checks an extension taken from File.basename(URI.parse(url).path) on the API path or the multipart filename — a user renames a 10MB non-image payload to .png, skips downsizing entirely (no size reduction, and ImageMagick never processes it), and uploads it with a self-declared content_type of image/png; the server-side max-image-size policy is defeated for any file with a spoofed extension, and the trust-the-client content_type flows into Upload.create_for.

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing block runs only when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true (based on the filename/URL path). The finding claims a user can rename a non-image payload to `.png` to *skip* downsizing, but spoofing an image extension would make `is_image?` more likely to return true, not bypass it. Also, whether a large file can be uploaded without downsizing depends on validations inside `Upload.create_for`, which are not shown in the diff, so the claim that the server-side max-image-size policy is “defeated” is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Hardcoding the client-side limit to 10MB bypasses the site's configured upload-size settings for all upload types, not just images. max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb (and any other per-type *_size_kb setting) are ignored client-side: on a site configured with max_attachment_size_kb = 512, users select attachments up to 10MB and push them at the server; combined with the server's downsizing only applying to image filenames, oversized non-image attachments that previously were rejected now transit the full upload path. An admin-configured control is silently disabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the per-type client-side size check was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB), and the 413 handler similarly hardcodes 10MB instead of `max_image_size_kb`. This verifiably ignores admin-configured `*_size_kb` limits client-side for all upload types, allowing users to attempt uploads above the configured limits (e.g., attachments) and only rely on server-side handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new public downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) signature interpolates a caller-supplied raw dimensions string into a shell command via convert_with's backticks, removing the structured width/height parameterization the old dimensions(width, height) builder provided. In this diff dimensions is the literal "80%" so it is safe today, but the method's contract change means any future caller that forwards user-influenced geometry (e.g. a user-specified crop or resize string) gets direct command injection into `#{instructions.join(" ")}`; the deletion of the width/height typed parameters is what creates the injection-shaped API.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `OptimizedImage.downsize` to ultimately accept a raw `dimensions` string (the last `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` overrides the earlier 4-arg version) and passes it into `*_instructions` which are executed via backticks in `convert_with` (`#{instructions.join(" ")}`). This removes the prior width/height-style API contract and allows arbitrary geometry strings like "80%" (now used by the new upload-downsizing loop), creating a direct shell-injection vector if any caller supplies untrusted dimensions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The file defines self.downsize twice (the 4-arg (max_width, max_height) version is immediately shadowed by the dimensions version), so existing callers passing separate width and height integers now hit the wrong parameterization. Any existing call site of OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 100) now binds dimensions=100 and opts=100 instead of building "100x100"; the mutated image paths this controls (thumbnails/resized avatars) silently corrupt geometry handling for the next maintainer who cannot tell which overload is live — a change-safety hazard the duplicate definition hides.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, `self.downsize` is defined twice: first as `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, then later redefined as `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later definition overwrites the earlier one, so existing call sites passing separate width/height (e.g., `downsize(from,to,100,100)`) will now bind `dimensions=100` and `opts=100`. This breaks `optimize` which expects `opts` to be a hash (it does `opts[:allow_animation]`), causing a runtime error (TypeError/NoMethodError) and/or incorrect geometry handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The API URL-download path fetches a user-supplied URL with only a size cap and rescue nil, and the diff widens that fetch budget from the configured max_image_size_kb to a fixed 10MB regardless of the site's setting. An API user triggers server-side fetches of arbitrary URLs (SSRF surface already present, but the budget is now decoupled from admin configuration), and the rescue nil swallows fetch failures leaving tempfile nil while filename/URI.parse(url) still runs on the raw user URL — a malformed URI raises after the rescue, producing a 500 on attacker-chosen input.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the API URL-download size limit from the configurable `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`uploads_controller.rb`), and similarly hardcodes client-side limits to `10 * 1024` KB in `utilities.js`, effectively ignoring admin-configured max upload sizes. This is a verifiable behavior/security regression (resource budget decoupled from configuration). Also, `FileHelper.download(... ) rescue nil` can yield `tempfile = nil` while `URI.parse(url)` is still executed unrescued, allowing malformed URLs to raise (the parse issue pre-existed but remains).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `downsize` is defined twice in the same class body; the second definition (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) silently overwrites the first (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}), so any existing caller still invoking the old 5-argument form mis-binds `max_height` into `opts` and `dimensions` becomes only the width string. Any out-of-diff caller doing OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 100) now executes downsize_instructions with dimensions="100" (height lost, opts={100 => true}), producing wrongly-sized optimized images with no error — a silent behavior regression in every existing downsize call site.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, `self.downsize` is defined twice in the same class body: first as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, then later again as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the latter definition overwrites the former, making the 5-argument form effectively removed. This is a real behavior change introduced by the diff and can break any existing callers still using the old `(max_width, max_height, opts)` signature (they will now hit an arity/type mismatch).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize but discards its return value, and convert_with returns false on ImageMagick failure, so the loop retries 5 times against the same unshrunk file and then falls through to Upload.create_for with an oversized tempfile. When ImageMagick fails (corrupt image, missing binary, unsupported format), the user waits through 5 pointless shell invocations and then receives a generic upload failure instead of the file_too_large message the client now promises at 10MB — the failure mode the loop was written to prevent still occurs, just slower.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop retries downsizing up to 5 times purely based on `tempfile.size` and never checks whether `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` succeeded. In optimized_image.rb, `downsize` ultimately calls `convert_with`, which returns `false` on ImageMagick failure; since that return value is ignored, a failure will cause up to 5 repeated no-op/failed conversions and then proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` with the same (still-oversized) tempfile. This is a real failure-mode regression (wasted retries and no early handling when downsizing cannot occur).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] downsize is invoked with `tempfile.path` as both `from` and `to` (in-place), so an ImageMagick run that fails midway overwrites/truncates the original tempfile before failure is detected. A partially-converted or zero-byte file is handed to Upload.create_for, which either fails with a confusing content-type/size error or stores a corrupted image — the user's original upload is destroyed by the very code meant to help them.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e. using the same file path for both input and output (in-place). `OptimizedImage.convert_with` runs an external command and only returns `false` on nonzero exit status, but the caller ignores this and proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with whatever is now on disk. If the ImageMagick conversion fails or partially writes, the original tempfile can be left corrupted/empty and the original upload content is lost, matching the finding’s data-loss/corruption concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client hardcodes `10 * 1024` as the max size, replacing the SiteSetting-driven value, so the client-side alert no longer reflects the server's actual `max_image_size_kb` (which can be any value, including 0 = unlimited). Admins who set max_image_size_kb above or below 10MB get a wrong number shown to every user; users uploading a 12MB image of a type not covered by the server downsize path (non-image, or max_image_size_kb == 0) pass the client check and then hit a server rejection with a mismatched error message.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the client-side max size check in `utilities.js` from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in both the pre-upload check and the 413 handler. This makes the client-side validation and alert text diverge from the server-configurable `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (including cases where it’s <10MB or 0/unlimited), causing incorrect UI messaging and potentially blocking uploads the server would accept or allowing uploads the server will later reject.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The API download branch names the tempfile `discourse-upload-#{type}` with no image extension, so inside `optimize` the animated-GIF detection `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` never matches for URL-provided uploads and `allow_animation` is silently ignored there. Animated GIFs downloaded via API URL take the non-animated instruction path, producing a still or wrongly-processed image with no error surfaced — a hidden branch divergence between file uploads and URL uploads that no test distinguishes.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new auto-downsize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the `_animated` instruction variant only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. In the API URL branch, the tempfile is created via `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`, which (as shown) provides no extension in the tempfile name/prefix, so `tempfile.path` will not necessarily end in `.gif` even if `filename` (parsed from the URL) is a GIF. That makes the `allow_animation` option effectively ignored for URL-provided GIFs during this downsize step, leading to different/incorrect processing for animated GIFs without an explicit error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The class now defines self.downsize twice — the original (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) version at ~line 146 is immediately shadowed by a new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version at ~line 150 — so every existing caller that invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts) with four positional arguments raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 4 for 3) because the last definition wins. Any pre-existing thumbnail-generation code path that calls downsize with the old 4-arg signature crashes at runtime with an unhandled ArgumentError instead of producing the resized image — thumbnail generation for those call sites is broken with no fallback.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb the diff leaves two `def self.downsize` definitions back-to-back: one taking `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then a later one taking `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later definition overrides the earlier one, so the 4-arg width/height version is effectively removed. While the finding’s exact arity error claim (“4 for 3”) isn’t accurate (the new method accepts 3 required + 1 optional), any existing call sites using the old signature (especially 5 args including opts, or 4 args where the 4th arg isn’t a hash) would now break at runtime (either ArgumentError for too many args, or mis-typed `opts` leading to errors when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side size check hard-codes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 instead of the site setting, so the composer rejects any file over 10MB with 'file too large' before the request is ever sent — but the entire point of the new server-side loop in uploads_controller.rb is to accept larger images and downsize them automatically. The feature is dead on arrival for its target users: a user uploading a 30MB image is blocked client-side by bootbox.alert and never reaches the server-side downsizing code; additionally, any site with max_image_size_kb above 10MB (or non-image types with larger limits) silently regresses — uploads the server previously accepted are now refused with a wrong limit shown in the error message.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the upload size limit was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in both the pre-upload check and the 413 handler. This means the client will block any upload over 10MB (and show 10MB in the error) regardless of configured site settings or upload type, preventing larger images (e.g. 30MB) from ever reaching the new server-side downsizing loop added in `uploads_controller.rb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...) with from == to — the same path is passed as both source and destination, so the ImageMagick command reads and writes the same file in place. ImageMagick's convert reading and writing the identical path can produce a truncated/corrupt output (the reader may consume the file while the writer truncates it), so the upload proceeds with a corrupted image or, if the convert fails outright, the original oversized file — either way the user gets a broken upload or a confusing file_too_large error after the loop silently exhausts all 5 attempts.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, passing the same filesystem path for both `from` and `to`. In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` delegates to `optimize(...)` which ultimately calls `convert_with(instructions, to)`, i.e., it runs an external ImageMagick convert command writing to `to`. Writing output to the same path as the input is a real correctness risk (in-place convert can corrupt/truncate or fail), and the loop also ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`, so failures would be silent and could leave an oversized or corrupted tempfile that then gets uploaded or triggers later errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loop ignores the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (convert_with returns false when the shell command exits non-zero) and performs no check after the loop, so a failing convert is retried four more times against the unchanged file and then execution falls through to Upload.create_for with the still-oversized tempfile. A corrupt or non-processable image that fails convert burns 5 shell invocations with no log and no early exit, then surfaces only as a generic 'file too large' error at upload creation — the operator gets no signal that downsizing itself failed, and the user sees a misleading error for what is actually an image-processing failure.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but ignores its boolean return value (via `OptimizedImage.optimize` -> `convert_with`, which returns `false` on non-zero exit). If the conversion fails, `tempfile.size` remains unchanged, so the `while ... tempfile.size > ...` condition stays true and the code will retry up to 5 times against the same oversized file, then fall through to `Upload.create_for(...)` without detecting/handling the downsizing failure. The diff also shows `convert_with` discards stderr/stdout (`&> /dev/null`), so failures are silent here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 413 response handler now hard-codes 10MB as the reported max size, disconnecting the displayed limit from the server's actual configured max_image_size_kb. Users on sites where max_image_size_kb differs from 10240 are shown a wrong limit in the file_too_large alert, misdirecting them about what they need to do to fix the upload.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js`, the 413 handler was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This will display an incorrect `max_size_kb` in the `file_too_large` alert on any site where `max_image_size_kb` is not 10240, directly matching the finding. The earlier client-side size check was also changed to the same hard-coded limit, further disconnecting behavior/messaging from configured settings.
